snapshot_note: php::print_r / php::var_dump OVER ANY MADC TYPE — THE ARC IS COMPLETE and RELEASED as v0.85.0 (session #104, 2026-08-18): all 20 probe shapes render, and the one remaining refusal is a principled limit that names itself. Both are declared in <ns_php> as function TEMPLATES with NO definition anywhere: "any type" has no signature a host could satisfy, so the CIR builder GENERATES the dumper for whatever type the argument has (src/cir_dump.cpp) and the runtime carries only output primitives (src/rt/rt_dump.c — strict C11, printf not std::cout, ledger-registered so a -static-libmadc Mach-O program that dumps still links). A program that never dumps carries nothing: no runtime type-descriptor table exists. That shape also makes the owner's "cannot be exported" constraint STRUCTURAL (a declared-but-undefined template is an unresolved symbol for any C++ host) and is the FIRST deliberate exception to cpp-first-api.md. Recognition is a TAG, never a name: FuncDef::inline_builtin_kind, stamped at declaration registration — the same carrier std::addressof / std::forward use, already serialized by the forest, so a PACKED <ns_php> keeps it. COVERED: scalars, C strings, structs/classes with access + inheritance, unions, anonymous unions, bit-fields, fixed and multidimensional arrays, char arrays as text, POSITIONAL containers (std::string, std::vector, std::array), POINTERS (followed, at the same depth, with PHP's *RECURSION* for a real cycle — a generated dumper FUNCTION per (pointee, flavor) plus a shared thread-local ANCESTOR STACK keyed on (address, TYPE)), ENUMS (enumerator name + real backing type, PHP 8.1's shape), ITERATOR CONTAINERS (std::map / std::set / std::list, plus any hand-rolled container with the same shape — class iterator or raw pointer iterator), the full madc::value / array nine-kind gamut through ONE runtime walk, and print_r($x, true) capture with a runtime flag. The iterator loop is COUNTED off size() because libstdc++ declares operator==/operator!= on every one of these iterators as friend FREE functions — findMethod cannot see a free function, so `it != c.end()` cannot be generated at all; that is why size() belongs to the recognizer and why a container with begin()/end() and NO size() is the one permanent refusal. The recognizer, class_iterator_iteration_protocol, lives in src/cir_builder.cpp beside its positional twin and is SHARED: the range-for is its second consumer, so `for (std::pair<const int,int> &kv : m)` works now too. PHP-oracled byte for byte against php-cli 8.3.6.

known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
